lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: 1. **Name base and head.** Use the refs the user named; three-dot (`base...head`) is the request or branch diff. When the user names a request, read its base branch, head ref, and the remote URL from the forge in one call; `git fetch <remote> <base> <head>` then goes first in the step-2 call, even when both refs exist locally, so a stale local ref cannot change the diff. When the change is already on the default branch, use the request's recorded base and head SHAs; the moving default-branch `HEAD` includes later merges. When only the head is known, base is its merge-base with the named base branch. A ref that is not in the clone gets `git fetch <remote> <ref>` first in the step-2 call, and the review uses the fetched refs. When the change is not committed, tell the user this review reads commits only, and ask them to commit or name a ref. A request whose base branch is the head branch of another request is in a stack: that branch (or its recorded base SHA once merged) is the base, so the review covers this layer only, and the lower request is a `pr` source, cited where a group uses its code. Done when both refs are chosen.

lines.text: The draft holds `mirrors-<n>` groups (files that received the same change), one `mechanical` group (renames, copies, moves, generated output), and one `change` group for the rest, all with stub prose. Its `size` is the CLI's guess from line counts. Trust the digest hints `same change as`, `pairs with`, and `replaces`; a file that `replaces` a deleted one, and the file it `replaced`, are a new version, not a move, and are read with their story. Done when the digest, the draft, the log, and each source to its end are in context.

lines.text: 3. **Read the change.** Run `npx comprehende@0.13.4 show --base <base> --head <head> --batch <n>` for each batch the digest's `read:` line names, one batch per call, until a batch ends with `# Last batch`. The CLI leaves out the files you can skip, and batch 1 lists them; read a skipped generated file with `show --file "<path>"` when its digest symbols show hand-written code. When your harness cuts a batch, read the rest from the file it saved, or fetch the cut hunks with one `show --hunk "<ref>"` per hunk, several per call; `show` reads only its first `--hunk`. Done when you have read every batch to its end.

lines.text: 4. **Group.** Start from the draft and apply Grouping. Keep a draft group that holds one concern. Merge draft groups that serve one concern, and split a group where a reader would stop and review the first piece alone. When a split or a merge is a close call, keep one group. Then name the stories (see Parts). Done when your reply names each story with its groups, or, for one story, says for each group why it could not have been its own PR.

lines.text: 5. **List the facts, then write.** Before the write call, list in your reply every fact the hunks and sources show. The list has no length limit and stays out of `review.json`. List each changed result with its cause and mechanism, each new test with its input and what fails without it, each move or helper with its old place, its callers, and what differs from the old code (a message, error, or result the old code gave that the new call does not), each file that breaks a repeated pattern, each fact the hunks alone do not show (a caller in another file, a value a source sets, a removed line with no effect, a new export nothing uses), each thing a source says about scope or a failing CI job, each judgment call, and each source item with its verdict (see lookFor). Check a claim about code outside the diff with one `git grep` batch at `<head>`. Then write the document from the list, one field at a time, by its section under Fields. Each fact has one home: a source divergence in `lookFor`, a judgment call in `attention`, a fact about one file in its file note, a result that spans files or a source's word on scope in the group `summary`, and a fact about one line in a note. Drop a fact only when it repeats another, or when it is your own bug report, nit, missing test, or refactor idea. Copy every ref from the draft into the group that holds it, verbatim; keep `version` and `source` from the draft. Write the whole file in one shell call, then validate:

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: restore the full fact list; drop the five-file group hint
lines.text: A group is one review concern: hunks a reviewer reads together and names in a phrase. A directory is a concern only when the directory itself is the point.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - **One user, one home.** Code sits with what only it serves: a unit test with the code it checks (the `pairs with` hint names the module), a one-line call site, declaration, or re-export with the code it serves, an option, flag, or setting with the code that reads it, a seed, helper, or short fixture with the one spec that uses it, also when its folder holds shared helpers. A new feature's code, seeds, helpers, and spec are one group. New code sits with the branch that selects it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - **Many users, one foundation.** A contract that several later groups build on sits in a foundation group with the files that define it, and the groups that use it `dependsOn` it. A helper or shared code that is not such a contract stays in the group of its first user; split it out only where a reader would stop and review it alone.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - **One pattern, one group.** The same kind of edit across many files, such as a migration or the adoption of a new helper, is one group, apart from the foundation it adopts. Do not split it by area.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - **Harnesses.** A new integration harness and the build or CI files that run it are one group, apart from the production code it exercises.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - **Fixtures.** Fixtures or golden files that pin cases of one change stay in one group, also when a case exercises its own branch: the group of the code they pin, or, when their changed lines in the digest outnumber that code's, one trailing group of its own. A case's own branch in the code stays with the rest of that code.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - **Mechanical work.** Renames, identifier-only edits, formatting, pure moves, and generated output form their own group. Check each file in the draft `mechanical` group: a file with a real behavior change moves to its story by its path. Output a generator or build step in the diff writes from code (a checked-in schema or client) is mechanical too, in its own group; its summary says whether the hunks match that code at head, and output that does not match is not safe to skip.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - **Mirrors.** A `mirrors-<n>` group merges into a larger group when other files serve the same concern with a different edit, such as the change that makes the repeated edit needed, or calls to the same new helper; that group's `summary` names the file the others repeat. Draft `mirrors-<n>` groups that repeat one kind of edit merge into one group.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - **Shared hunks.** A hunk may sit in several groups when it matters to more than one story. A group that holds a hunk with two concerns names both.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: ### Parts

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: A story is work that could have been its own PR, approved alone. Each story is a `part`: a short name on every group of that story, with one document `parts[]` entry (`name`, and a one-sentence `summary`). One story means no `part` and no `parts`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - A story holds what it needs to be approved: its foundation, tests, enabling renames, and docs. The layers a feature needs to work (a contract, its client, its server, its UI) are one story, even when they could ship as stacked PRs. Work that builds on the feature and that the rest of the change does not need, such as authoring tools, templates, or a demo app, is a story of its own. A foundation carries the `part` of the story that first uses it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A shared motive (one ticket that lists unrelated items, a cleanup sweep, a retro) gives the document one `why`; the work under it can still be several stories. One cause fixed in several places is one story.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - Unasked work is a story of its own: a dependency policy change (exact versions to ranges, or back), a standalone document, a refactor the asked work does not need, production code in a PR about tests. Unasked work that only enables the asked story (path renames, fixture layout, local startup) stays in that story.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: tie-break grouping and parts choices for consistent reviews
lines.text: - Docs and agent notes about a story's own feature stay in that story. Small edits of one kind for one reader on other topics, such as several notes in agent docs, are one story.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A mechanical group that exists only because of a story is that story's last group, with nothing depending on it. One that could have been its own PR is its own part.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: ### Order, size, and refs

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - `dependsOn` names an earlier group the reader needs to understand this one, inside the same part. Independent parts have none.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - `suggestedOrder` walks the whole review: inside a story, contracts and foundations, then call sites, then mechanical work; across stories, a part another story builds on comes first, and mechanical parts, standalone docs, and test-only cleanup go last.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - Document `size` is human review burden: `trivial`, `small`, `medium`, `large`, `very-large`. Judge the burden yourself; the draft's guess counts lines only, and the length of this review does not change it: forty files with one import change are `small`; a new component plus follow-ups across screens is `medium`; a new contract that later groups depend on is `large`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - Coverage: every live hunk sits in at least one group. A path covers every hunk of its file, and a path ending in `/` covers every hunk under that directory that no other ref names. To move one file out of a directory ref, put its path in the other group. When a file is split across groups, name each hunk as `path@oldStart+newStart` (`old/path -> new/path@oldStart+newStart` for a renamed hunk), with the numbers from the digest or from the `@@` header `show` prints. Image files are paths. Lockfiles have no refs. Never invent a ref.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Optional fields, each written only as its section below says. Document: `why`, `lookFor` (array of strings), `parts`, `sources`. Group: `why`, `part`, `sources` (ids), `attention` (`kind`, `note`), `questions` (array of one string), `focus` (array of `path`, `side`, `start`, `end`, `caption`), `notes` (array of `path`, `side`, `line`, `body`), `fileNotes` (object from path to one line), `dependsOn` (group ids). `side` is `new` for a line of the head file and `old` for a line of the base file. Every line number comes from `show` output.

lines.author: Cursor Agent

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Document `title` is a short name for the whole change. Keep the human's title (request, ticket, or transcript) when it is descriptive and names this change; otherwise write one. A branch slug, "WIP", or "fix" is not a title.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.summary: Always write a whole-change what; skip Overview Why when silent.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Document `summary` is one sentence naming what the change is, two for a mixed PR that names its stories. A part `summary` is the one-sentence what of that story.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.summary: Always write a whole-change what; skip Overview Why when silent.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Group `summary` is one easy sentence saying what the group does and how its hunks relate: "The route in `routes.ts` calls the new validator in `core.ts`.", not a file list. A result that spans several files, or a source's word on scope, adds a second sentence; other facts go in file notes, or, in a one-file group, a further sentence. A `mirrors-<n>` or `mechanical` summary says what the reader can skip and why that is safe, and a `mirrors-<n>` summary also says what the repeated change does.

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.summary: Always write a whole-change what; skip Overview Why when silent.

lines.text: ### Why and sources

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.summary: Add per-story summaries under Overview part headers.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Document `why` is the problem or goal a source states, in one or two sentences in the source's own terms, plus who hits it when the source says, with no cause, benefit, or reader need the source does not name. Find that source sentence first ("Support SSO login", "retries flood the API"). A sentence that only says what the change does belongs in the summary. With no such sentence, or two unrelated stories and no unifying source, omit the why.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.summary: Remove generate so grouping stays with the agent, and keep the skill schema a copy of the CLI contract.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Group `why` holds a reason a source states for this group that the document `why` and the group `summary` do not give. Most groups omit it: a one-group review, a group that serves the document `why`, a mechanical group, and a foundation group, whose `dependsOn` already shows what it enables. A part no source asks for says so: "No source asks for this dependency change."

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Each source you use is a `sources` item with a short `id` (`s1`), a `kind`, a `label`, and `url`, `title`, `gist`, and `part` when you have them. Put its id on the `sources` array of each group that uses it. Cite in prose with `[text](source:s1)`, where the link text is words the sentence already needs (`[#24](source:s1) asks for a retry`), one citation per sentence, and only for a sentence that source says.

lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - `pr-comment`: one per comment the prose cites or pins, label `alice on PR #32`, with `author` and `body` copied. A comment that asked for code the change has at head is the first source of that code: cite it in the group that holds that code, also when the request body or a reply repeats the outcome. Pin a comment (`path`, `side`, `line`) when its thread is open, it is not outdated, and the forge reports a current line at head. A conversation comment has no pin.

lines.author: Máté Molnár

lines.text: ### lookFor

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.summary: Teach mechanical layers, reserved lookFor, and shorter review prose.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Document `lookFor` holds the divergences between the sources and the code at head. Source items are each requirement and acceptance item in a ticket, each behavior claim in the request description and commit subjects, and each request in a review comment. Test plans, QA notes, and out-of-scope lists are context, except a test name or count that differs at head. Give each item a verdict: done as asked, done differently, not done, or not true at head. Each verdict other than done as asked is one bullet: what the source says, what the hunks show, and the reason when a source or the code gives one, or that no source gives one. When a later source overrides an earlier one, the bullet names both. A manual step a source says the change needs (a setting, a migration) is also a bullet, and so is an instruction a source gives a reviewer or an agent (see Why and sources). Each bullet is a fact true at head, with a citation; pseudocode, diagrams, collapsed diffs, commit lists, hunk counts, and pass/fail marks stay out. Omit the field when nothing needs a bullet.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: apply the writing review

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Group `attention` is the one judgment call a reviewer makes in this group: what the code at head does, where it matters, and the decision. `kind` is `contract` (a promise callers rely on), `tradeoff` (a cost accepted for a gain), `product` (a product or scope call), or `risk` (a risk accepted). The `note` is two or three sentences, true at head, on hunks you read. Typical calls:

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill, glossary, and eval: attention plus document lookFor

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A change callers see, such as equality or identity: `contract`, with a predicted trace (a small input, where old and new paths diverge, the observable result).

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A workaround (a sleep, a forced write, a retry): `tradeoff`, saying what the app does without it.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - Application code in a PR whose sources are about tests, CI, or tooling: `product`, naming the behavior change.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A setup or teardown script that deletes or overwrites a file that is not test output: `risk`, naming the path, when, and what the developer loses.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A behavior change no source mentions: the kind it asks for.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Two calls in one group mean two concerns: split the group, or keep the one that weighs most. Most groups have none, including renames, formatting, wording-only docs, mirrors, and mechanical groups. A bug, a missing test, a nit, a refactor idea, or a point settled in review is not an attention. A fact that needs no decision goes in the `summary`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Add group intent questions with an Ask agent button

lines.text: ### Questions

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Add group intent questions with an Ask agent button

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Group `questions` holds at most one question about intent, when the code and the sources leave the reason for a choice a hunk shows open. It asks for the author's reason; a bug, a missing test, or a nit stays out. One sentence that names the symbol and the choice: "Why does the helper set `SameSite=Lax` and not `Strict`?". When a source answers it, the answer goes in `why` instead. The UI turns each question into a prompt for the agent that wrote the change. Most groups have none.

lines.text: ### Focus and notes

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Focus ranges and line notes inside hunks

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: Write a `focus` range for a hunk longer than 25 lines whose concern sits in part of it: at most 25 lines inside one live hunk of its group, on the lines that carry that concern; on removed code its `side` is `old`. In a test, those are the call under test and its assertions; setup stays outside. An added file gets no range. The `caption` is one sentence on what to check there.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Focus ranges and line notes inside hunks

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: A `note` pins one sentence to one line inside a hunk of its group: what the code alone does not say, such as a caller in another file, the source that sets a value, or why a line that looks wrong is right. At most three per group; most have none. Each caption and note adds a fact the `summary` and `attention` do not state.

lines.text: Each file of a group with two or more files gets a `fileNotes` line, keyed by its path (the new path for a rename, never a directory). A one-file group has none. The line says what changed in that file, not what the file does, and states a fact the group `summary` does not:

lines.text: - A changed result: the old and the new result, and the call that gives it. A changed message, error, or scope counts, also inside a refactor or a move. "Parses with `urlsplit`, so `[::1]` gives host `::1`, not an error."

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A test or fixture: the input and what fails without the change. "Runs a request against `[::1]:8080`; raised `ValueError` before."

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A helper or a move: the old place and what differs. "Moved from `App.tsx`; adds `compact` padding."

lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: - A generated, mechanical, or repeated file: a short label. "Same rename as `server.ts`."

lines.text: ## Write the prose

lines.author: Cursor Agent
lines.summary: Teach mechanical layers, reserved lookFor, and shorter review prose.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: rewrite for one place per rule; read by batch; terse fact list
lines.text: All prose is for a tired engineer on the first read, with the diff one click away. Spend words on `lookFor` verdicts first, then attentions with their traces, then file notes, then notes. A fact appears once, in the field that fits it. Most fields come in under these usual lengths; only a complex change runs longer, and a field with nothing to say is omitted.
